newsitem.title: INDIA: Oil India to dilute government stake in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Oil India to dilute government stake in 1997/98.

text.p: The state-run Oil India Ltd (OIL) plans to divest part of its equity now held by the government in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), its chairman said.
"We are thinking of divesting between five to 10 percent this fiscal," OIL chairman N.N. Gogoi told Reuters on Tuesday.
"The divestment commission will meet us soon," he said.
The divestment commission is a government panel which advises government on divestment strategy.
Gogoi said the divestment of the government stake will be followed up by a public issue of shares.
Depending on the public response, OIL may tap the international equity market at a later date, he said.
Five merchant banks have been identified to manage the proposed share issue, he said.
Gogoi said OIL's fund requirement during the Ninth Plan period which runs for five years from April 1, 1997 was earlier estimated at about 10 billion rupees
"This means 2.0 billion rupees each year. We don't need so much funds now," he said.
OIL is now 97 percent owned by the government, with the remaining three percent held by its employees.
OIL is India's second largest oil producer after the state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation.
